concept.title: Piecewise Polynomial Cap-Volume Conjecture for Convex Polytopes
concept.concept_description: For any full-dimensional convex polytope P in R^d, the cap-volume function V(H) = vol(P ∩ H⁺), mapping an oriented hyperplane H to the volume of the cap it cuts from P, is piecewise polynomial of degree exactly d on each full-dimensional cell of the arrangement induced by the vertices of P in the dual space of oriented hyperplanes. This strengthens the paper's key observation that V is piecewise rational to the sharper claim that it is piecewise polynomial, with the degree bound d arising from the fact that cap vertices on the hyperplane vary linearly in the hyperplane parameters while simplex volumes are degree-d polynomials in vertex coordinates.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any full-dimensional convex polytope P in R^d, the cap-volume function V(H) = vol(P ∩ H⁺), mapping an oriented hyperplane H to the volume of the cap it cuts from P, is piecewise polynomial of degree exactly d on each full-dimensional cell of the arrangement induced by the vertices of P in the dual space of oriented hyperplanes. This strengthens the paper's key observation that V is piecewise rational to the sharper claim that it is piecewise polynomial, with the degree bound d arising from the fact that cap vertices on the hyperplane vary linearly in the hyperplane parameters while simplex volumes are degree-d polynomials in vertex coordinates.
concept.lean_guess: Fix a full-dimensional cell C of the arrangement in the dual space where the combinatorial type of the cap P ∩ H⁺ is constant. Within C, the vertices of the cap are either original vertices of P (constant) or intersection points of edges of P with H. Show that these intersection points vary linearly in the hyperplane parameters on C. Triangulate the cap into simplices; each simplex volume is a degree-d polynomial in its vertex coordinates. Since each vertex is either constant or linear in the hyperplane parameters, each simplex volume is a degree-d polynomial in the hyperplane parameters on C. Summing over simplices yields a degree-d polynomial for the total cap volume on C. Genericity arguments show the degree is exactly d, not less.

normalized state-counting function with a large number of contributing degrees of
freedom — the properly centred and scaled maximum converges in distribution to

  maximum of `n` independent copies) reproduces the same law up to a
  deterministic shift by `log n` — the fixed-point property that singles `G` out.

conjecture, random-matrix universality classes and Gaussian log-correlated fields,
for all of which `G` is the conjectured (and in several cases proven) limit law of
the recentred maximum.
-/

open Real Filter Topology

namespace BlackHoleGumbel

/-- The Gumbel cumulative distribution function `G(x) = exp(-exp(-x))`. -/
noncomputable def gumbelCdf (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-Real.exp (-x))

/-- The Gumbel probability density `g(x) = e^{-x} · G(x)`. -/
noncomputable def gumbelPdf (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-x) * gumbelCdf x

/-- The Gumbel CDF is strictly positive. -/
theorem gumbelCdf_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < gumbelCdf x := Real.exp_pos _

/-- The Gumbel CDF is strictly below `1`. -/
theorem gumbelCdf_lt_one (x : ℝ) : gumbelCdf x < 1 := by
  rw [gumbelCdf, show (1 : ℝ) = Real.exp 0 by simp]
  exact Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by simpa using Real.exp_pos (-x))

/-- The Gumbel CDF is strictly increasing: it is a genuine distribution function. -/
theorem gumbelCdf_strictMono : StrictMono gumbelCdf := by
  intro a b hab
  simp only [gumbelCdf]
  exact Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by simpa using Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by simpa using hab))

theorem gumbelCdf_tendsto_atTop : Tendsto gumbelCdf atTop (nhds 1) := by
  have : Tendsto (fun x => -Real.exp (-x)) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    simpa using (Real.tendsto_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero).neg
  simpa [gumbelCdf] using (Real.continuous_exp.tendsto 0).comp this

theorem gumbelCdf_tendsto_atBot : Tendsto gumbelCdf atBot (nhds 0) := by
  have h2 : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-x)) atBot atTop :=
    Real.tendsto_exp_atTop.comp tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop
  have h3 : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => -Real.exp (-x)) atBot atBot :=
    tendsto_neg_atTop_atBot.comp h2
  simpa [gumbelCdf] using (Real.tendsto_exp_atBot).comp h3

/-- **Max-stability functional equation.** Raising the Gumbel law to the `n`-th
power — the law of the maximum of `n` independent copies — reproduces the same
law shifted by `log n`: `G(x)^n = G(x - log n)`.  This fixed-point property is
what distinguishes `G` among all extreme-value limit laws. -/
theorem gumbelCdf_maxStable (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (gumbelCdf x) ^ n = gumbelCdf (x - Real.log n) := by
  simp only [gumbelCdf, ← Real.exp_nat_mul]
  rw [neg_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, Real.exp_add, Real.exp_log (by positivity)]
  ring_nf

/-- **Extreme-value convergence to the Gumbel law.** The recentred maximum of `n`
independent unit-exponential contributions has cumulative distribution
`(1 - e^{-x}/n)^n`, which converges to `G(x)` as `n → ∞`. -/
theorem gumbel_extreme_limit (x : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (1 - Real.exp (-x) / n) ^ n) atTop (nhds (gumbelCdf x)) := by
  have := Real.tendsto_one_add_div_pow_exp (-Real.exp (-x))
  simp only [gumbelCdf]
  convert this using 2 with n
  ring

/-- The Gumbel CDF is differentiable with derivative equal to the Gumbel density
`g(x) = e^{-x} · G(x)`. -/
theorem gumbelCdf_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt gumbelCdf (gumbelPdf x) x := by
  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun x => -Real.exp (-x)) (Real.exp (-x)) x := by
    simpa using ((Real.hasDerivAt_exp (-x)).comp x ((hasDerivAt_id x).neg)).neg
  have := (Real.hasDerivAt_exp (-Real.exp (-x))).comp x h1
  simp only [gumbelPdf, gumbelCdf] at *
  convert this using 1
  ring

/-- The Gumbel density is strictly positive everywhere. -/
theorem gumbelPdf_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < gumbelPdf x :=
  mul_pos (Real.exp_pos _) (gumbelCdf_pos x)

/-- The Gumbel density is bounded above by its modal value `e^{-1}`. -/
theorem gumbelPdf_le_mode (x : ℝ) : gumbelPdf x ≤ Real.exp (-1) := by
  simp only [gumbelPdf, gumbelCdf]
  have hu : Real.exp (-x) ≤ Real.exp (Real.exp (-x) - 1) := by
    have := Real.add_one_le_exp (Real.exp (-x) - 1); linarith
  calc Real.exp (-x) * Real.exp (-Real.exp (-x))

    _ = Real.exp (-1) := by rw [← Real.exp_add]; ring_nf

In a well-founded poset, the height function h(x) = the ordinal rank of x (defined via well-founded recursion: h(x) = sup {h(y)+1 : y < x}) takes values in ordinals. 1. **Ordinal height**: For x : P, define `height x` via WellFounded.fix on the well-founded relation `<`. Concretely: `height x = ⨆ (y < x), height y + 1`. This maps P into ordinals.

4. **Maximal chain construction**: Using the axiom of choice (or `Classical.choice`), select one element from each nonempty level. - `height_strict_mono`: x < y → height x < height y (NOT x ≤ y → height x ≤ height y, which is weaker; the strict version is what makes levels antichains)

# The Aharoni–Korman property for finite (well-founded, FAC) posets

The **Aharoni–Korman conjecture** asserts that every partially ordered set with no
infinite antichain admits a chain `C` together with a partition of the whole order
into antichains such that `C` meets every part of the partition.

Well-founded posets satisfying the *finite antichain condition* (FAC) form the natural
setting for the conjecture: well-foundedness rules out infinite descending chains and
FAC rules out infinite antichains.  Every finite poset is a (very special) instance of
this class, and here we establish the conjecture unconditionally for all finite posets.

The construction is via **height levels**.  In a finite poset the height function
`x ↦ height x` (the length of the longest chain with top `x`) is finite-valued.  Its
level sets `{x | height x = n}` are antichains, are pairwise disjoint, and cover the
order; a maximal chain rising to an element of maximal height meets every nonempty
level.  This yields an explicit Aharoni–Korman witness.

## Main results

* `AharoniKorman.levelSet_isAntichain` — each height level is an antichain.
* `AharoniKorman.chain_inter_antichain_subsingleton` — a chain and an antichain meet in
  at most one point.
* `AharoniKorman.finite_hasAharoniKorman` — every finite poset has an Aharoni–Korman
  witness.
* `AharoniKorman.finite_fac` and `AharoniKorman.finite_wellFoundedLT` — finite posets
  are FAC and well-founded, placing the main theorem inside the conjecture's setting.

## Lab Notes

`-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--`

* **Hypothesis.** The Aharoni–Korman conjecture, open in general, should hold with an
  *explicit* witness for every finite poset — and the witness should be describable
  purely through the height function, side-stepping any transfinite machinery.
* **Experiment.** Formalize the height-level construction: define the natural-number
  height, prove its level sets are antichains that partition the order, and exhibit a
  maximal chain (the underlying set of a longest strict series) hitting each level.
* **Analysis.** The construction works because in a finite poset height is finite,
  strictly monotone, and *surjective onto an initial segment* of `ℕ`: a longest chain
  passes through every height value `0, 1, …, H`, so it meets every nonempty level.
* **Critique.** The empty poset is a genuine corner case (no maximal element); it is
  handled separately with the empty witness. The partition is required to consist of
  *nonempty* antichains, so that "the chain meets every part" is a nonvacuous demand.
* **Synthesis.** `finite_hasAharoniKorman` packages the witness; `finite_fac` and

  class (well-founded, finite antichains).

namespace AharoniKorman

variable {α : Type*} [PartialOrder α]

/-- An **antichain partition** of a poset: a family of nonempty antichains that are
pairwise disjoint and cover the whole order. -/
structure IsAntichainPartition (𝒜 : Set (Set α)) : Prop where
  antichains : ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) A
  covers : ∀ x, ∃ A ∈ 𝒜, x ∈ A
  disjoint : 𝒜.PairwiseDisjoint id

  ∃ (C : Set α) (𝒜 : Set (Set α)),
    IsChain (· ≤ ·) C ∧ IsAntichainPartition 𝒜 ∧ ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, (C ∩ A).Nonempty

/-! ### A chain meets an antichain in at most one point -/

/-- A chain and an antichain intersect in at most one element. This is the elementary
"dual" fact underpinning Dilworth/Mirsky-type theory. -/
theorem chain_inter_antichain_subsingleton {C A : Set α}
    (hC : IsChain (· ≤ ·) C) (hA : IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) A) :
    (C ∩ A).Subsingleton := by
  intro a ha b hb
  by_contra hne
  rcases hC ha.1 hb.1 hne with h | h
  · exact hA ha.2 hb.2 hne h
  · exact hA hb.2 ha.2 (Ne.symm hne) h

/-! ### Height in a finite poset -/

/-- In a finite poset every element has finite height. -/
theorem height_lt_top_of_finite [Fintype α] (x : α) : height x < ⊤ := by
  refine lt_of_le_of_lt (Order.height_le (n := (Fintype.card α : ℕ∞)) ?_) (WithTop.coe_lt_top _)
  intro p _
  exact_mod_cast p.length_lt_card.le

/-- The natural-number valued height in a finite poset. -/
noncomputable def natHeight [Fintype α] (x : α) : ℕ := (height x).toNat

/-- `natHeight` really is the height, viewed in `ℕ∞`. -/
theorem coe_natHeight [Fintype α] (x : α) : (natHeight x : ℕ∞) = height x :=
  ENat.coe_toNat (height_lt_top_of_finite x).ne

/-- Height is strictly monotone in a finite poset. -/
theorem natHeight_lt_of_lt [Fintype α] {x y : α} (h : x < y) :
    natHeight x < natHeight y := by
  have h_height : height x < height y := height_strictMono h (height_lt_top_of_finite x)
  rw [← coe_natHeight x, ← coe_natHeight y, ENat.coe_lt_coe] at h_height
  exact h_height

/-! ### Height levels -/

/-- The `n`-th height level: the set of elements of height exactly `n`. -/
def levelSet [Fintype α] (n : ℕ) : Set α := {x | natHeight x = n}

/-- Every height level is an antichain: two elements of equal height are incomparable. -/
theorem levelSet_isAntichain [Fintype α] (n : ℕ) :
    IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) (levelSet (α := α) n) := by
  intro x hx y hy hxy hle
  have hlt : x < y := lt_of_le_of_ne hle hxy
  have := natHeight_lt_of_lt hlt
  rw [(show natHeight x = n from hx), (show natHeight y = n from hy)] at this
  exact lt_irrefl n this

/-- Distinct height levels are disjoint. -/
theorem levelSet_disjoint [Fintype α] {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≠ n) :
    Disjoint (levelSet (α := α) m) (levelSet (α := α) n) :=
  Set.disjoint_left.mpr fun _ hxm hxn => h <| hxm.symm.trans hxn

/-- The family of nonempty height levels. -/
def levelPartition (α : Type*) [PartialOrder α] [Fintype α] : Set (Set α) :=
  {A | ∃ n, A = levelSet (α := α) n ∧ (levelSet (α := α) n).Nonempty}

/-- The nonempty height levels form an antichain partition of a finite poset. -/
theorem isAntichainPartition_levelPartition [Fintype α] :
    IsAntichainPartition (levelPartition α) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rintro A ⟨n, rfl, -⟩
    exact levelSet_isAntichain n
  · exact fun x => ⟨_, ⟨natHeight x, rfl, ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩, rfl⟩
  · rintro A ⟨n, rfl, -⟩ B ⟨m, rfl, -⟩ hAB
    exact levelSet_disjoint (fun h => hAB (by rw [h]))
  · rintro A ⟨n, rfl, hn⟩
    exact hn

/-! ### The main theorem -/

/-- **Aharoni–Korman for finite posets.** Every finite poset admits a chain and a
partition into antichains such that the chain meets every part. -/
theorem finite_hasAharoniKorman [Fintype α] : HasAharoniKorman α := by
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty α with hα | hα
  · exact ⟨∅, ∅, IsChain.empty,
      ⟨by simp, fun x => (hα.false x).elim, by simp, by simp⟩, by simp⟩
  · obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := Finite.exists_max (natHeight : α → ℕ)
    have hht : height x₀ = (natHeight x₀ : ℕ∞) := (coe_natHeight x₀).symm
    obtain ⟨p, hp_last, hp_len⟩ := exists_series_of_height_eq_coe x₀ hht
    -- The strict series passes through every height value `0, 1, …, p.length`.
    have hidx : ∀ i : Fin (p.length + 1), natHeight (p.toFun i) = (i : ℕ) := by
      intro i
      have he : height (p.toFun i) = ((i : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by
        apply height_eq_index_of_length_eq_height_last
        rw [hp_last, hp_len, coe_natHeight]
      rw [← coe_natHeight] at he
      exact_mod_cast he
    refine ⟨Set.range p.toFun, levelPartition α, ?_,
      isAntichainPartition_levelPartition, ?_⟩
    · rintro a ⟨i, rfl⟩ b ⟨j, rfl⟩ -
      rcases le_total i j with h | h
      · exact Or.inl (p.strictMono.monotone h)
      · exact Or.inr (p.strictMono.monotone h)
    · rintro A ⟨n, rfl, z, hz⟩
      have hzn : natHeight z = n := hz
      have hn_le : n ≤ p.length := by
        rw [hp_len, ← hzn]; exact hx₀ z
      refine ⟨p.toFun ⟨n, by omega⟩, ⟨⟨n, by omega⟩, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
      show natHeight (p.toFun ⟨n, by omega⟩) = n
      simpa using hidx ⟨n, by omega⟩

/-! ### The finite poset lies in the conjecture's setting -/

/-- A finite poset satisfies the finite antichain condition: every antichain is finite. -/
theorem finite_fac [Finite α] {A : Set α} (_ : IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) A) : A.Finite :=
  Set.toFinite A

/-- A finite poset is well-founded, so it carries no infinite descending chain. -/
theorem finite_wellFoundedLT [Finite α] : WellFoundedLT α :=
  Finite.to_wellFoundedLT

end AharoniKorman

# Computational Evidence — Aharoni–Korman for finite posets

We investigate the claim: *every finite poset admits a chain `C` and a partition of
the order into (nonempty) antichains such that `C` meets every part.*

The construction under test is the **height-level partition**: assign to each element
`x` its height `h(x)` (length of the longest chain topped by `x`), group elements by
height into levels `L_0, L_1, …, L_H`, and take as chain the underlying set of a
longest strictly increasing chain.

## Small-case calculations

* **Antichain (width `w`, height `0`).** Every element has height `0`; the single
  level `L_0` is the whole poset, and any one-point chain meets it. Witness size: 1
  part, chain length 1. ✓

* **Chain of length `n`.** Heights are `0, 1, …, n-1`; each level is a singleton, and
  the whole chain meets every level. Witness: `n` parts, chain length `n`. ✓

* **Diamond `{⊥, a, b, ⊤}`** with `⊥ < a, b < ⊤` and `a, b` incomparable.
  Heights: `h(⊥)=0`, `h(a)=h(b)=1`, `h(⊤)=2`. Levels: `{⊥}, {a,b}, {⊤}`. A maximal
  chain `⊥ < a < ⊤` meets all three levels. ✓ The two-element level `{a,b}` is a
  genuine antichain, so this is not a chain in disguise.

* **Two-layer bipartite order** `{a_1,a_2} < {b_1,b_2}` (all `a_i < b_j`).
  Heights: `a_i ↦ 0`, `b_j ↦ 1`. Levels `{a_1,a_2}` and `{b_1,b_2}`; chain
  `a_1 < b_1` meets both. ✓

## Counterexample hunt

The only structural risk is the **empty poset**: there is no maximal element to anchor
the chain. The empty witness (`C = ∅`, empty partition) satisfies every requirement
vacuously, and this case is discharged separately in the formal proof. No finite poset
was found that violates the height-level construction — indeed the argument shows none
can exist: heights realise a contiguous block `0, 1, …, H`, and a longest chain visits
each value exactly once.

## Table: witness parameters

| poset             | #levels (H+1) | max antichain | longest chain |
|-------------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| antichain (w pts) | 1             | w             | 1             |
| chain (n pts)     | n             | 1             | n             |
| diamond           | 3             | 2             | 3             |
| 2×2 bipartite     | 2             | 2             | 2             |

In every finite case the number of levels equals the length of a longest chain, and
that chain meets each level in exactly one point (a chain meets an antichain in at most
one point). This matches the formal lemma `chain_inter_antichain_subsingleton`.

# Future Directions — the Aharoni–Korman property beyond finiteness

The finite case establishes an *explicit* Aharoni–Korman witness built from the height
function. The following conjectures push the same structural idea toward the well-founded
and infinite regimes, where the conjecture is genuinely hard.

## 1. Height-level witnesses for well-founded FAC posets

**Conjecture.** Every well-founded poset with no infinite antichain admits an
Aharoni–Korman witness whose antichain partition is exactly the family of ordinal
height levels `{x : height x = ξ}` for ordinals `ξ`.

The key insight is that well-foundedness lets height take values in the ordinals rather
than merely in `ℕ`, and a *maximal* chain still climbs through a contiguous block of
height values, so it meets every nonempty level exactly once. Why now? The finite result
shows the level partition is the right object and that "a chain meets an antichain in at
most one point" forces the witness to be tight; the only missing ingredient is a
transfinite selection of the climbing chain, which well-foundedness supplies.

## 2. Boundedness of height across the FAC boundary

**Conjecture.** A countable poset satisfies the finite antichain condition if and only
if every element has finite height *and* only finitely many elements share each height.

The key insight is that FAC forbids infinite antichains, and each height level is itself
an antichain, so FAC and level-finiteness are two faces of the same constraint. Why now?
The finite theory already proves each level is an antichain and that distinct levels are
disjoint; promoting "each level finite" to a characterization of FAC turns a corollary
into a testable dichotomy.

## 3. Exactness of the level count

**Conjecture.** For a poset of finite height, the minimum number of antichains in any
Aharoni–Korman partition equals one more than the length of a longest chain, and this
minimum is achieved by the height-level partition.

The key insight is Mirsky-type duality: a chain meets each antichain at most once, so the
chain length lower-bounds the number of parts, while the height levels realise that bound.
Why now? The finite construction produces a witness in which chain length and part count
coincide, making the extremal identity concrete and checkable on every finite example.

## 4. Stability under products

**Conjecture.** If two well-founded FAC posets each admit a height-level Aharoni–Korman
witness, then their product (with the componentwise order) does as well, with height
equal to the sum of the coordinate heights.

The key insight is that height is additive along independent coordinates, so the product's
levels are "diagonal" sums of the factors' levels and inherit the antichain property. Why
now? With the single-factor witness pinned down by the height function, additivity of
height is the one structural fact needed to lift the construction to products, and it is
already visible in the finite calculations.
